label: Learn the Basics
desc: Core concepts of relational databases and the SQL language — where every journey starts.

subs.label: What are Relational Databases?
subs.desc: Tables, rows, columns, and the relational model introduced by Edgar Codd.

subs.label: RDBMS Benefits & Limitations
subs.desc: ACID properties, scalability trade-offs, and when to choose a relational DB.

subs.label: SQL Keywords
subs.desc: Reserved words: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, HAVING, etc.

subs.label: SQL vs NoSQL Databases
subs.desc: When to use relational vs document, key-value, column, or graph databases.

subs.label: Data Types
subs.desc: INT, VARCHAR, TEXT, DATE, TIMESTAMP, BOOLEAN, DECIMAL, and vendor-specific types.

subs.label: Operators
subs.desc: Arithmetic, comparison, logical (AND/OR/NOT), BETWEEN, IN, LIKE, IS NULL.

label: Basic SQL Syntax
desc: The fundamental SELECT statement and its clauses — how to read data from tables.

subs.label: SELECT
subs.desc: Retrieving columns, using aliases, DISTINCT, and selecting all with *.

subs.label: FROM
subs.desc: Specifying source tables, table aliases, and schema-qualified names.

subs.label: WHERE
subs.desc: Filtering rows with conditions — combining predicates with AND/OR.

subs.label: ORDER BY
subs.desc: Sorting results ASC/DESC, sorting by multiple columns and expressions.

subs.label: GROUP BY
subs.desc: Grouping rows that have the same values in specified columns.

subs.label: HAVING
subs.desc: Filtering grouped results — the WHERE clause for aggregated data.

subs.label: JOINs
subs.desc: Combining rows from two or more tables based on related columns.

label: Data Definition Language (DDL)
desc: Commands that define and modify the database schema — structure, not data.

subs.label: CREATE TABLE
subs.desc: Defining columns, data types, constraints, and default values.

subs.label: ALTER TABLE
subs.desc: Adding, dropping, and modifying columns; renaming tables.

subs.label: DROP TABLE
subs.desc: Permanently removing a table and all its data from the database.

subs.label: TRUNCATE TABLE
subs.desc: Removing all rows quickly without logging individual row deletions.

label: Data Manipulation Language (DML)
desc: Commands for inserting, updating, and deleting data in tables.

subs.label: INSERT
subs.desc: Adding new rows — single row, multi-row, and INSERT … SELECT patterns.

subs.label: UPDATE
subs.desc: Modifying existing rows — always use WHERE to avoid full-table updates.

subs.label: DELETE
subs.desc: Removing rows — differences between DELETE, TRUNCATE, and DROP.

label: Aggregate Queries
desc: Computing summary statistics across groups of rows.

subs.label: COUNT
subs.desc: COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col) — handling NULLs in aggregation.

subs.label: SUM
subs.desc: Summing numeric columns, using with COALESCE for NULL safety.

subs.label: AVG
subs.desc: Arithmetic mean — note that AVG ignores NULLs automatically.

subs.label: MIN
subs.desc: Finding the smallest value in a column or expression.

subs.label: MAX
subs.desc: Finding the largest value in a column or expression.

label: Data Constraints
desc: Rules enforced by the database engine to maintain data integrity.

subs.label: Primary Key
subs.desc: Uniquely identifies each row — auto-increment, composite keys.

subs.label: Foreign Key
subs.desc: Referential integrity — CASCADE, SET NULL, RESTRICT actions.

subs.label: UNIQUE
subs.desc: Ensures no duplicate values in a column or column combination.

subs.label: NOT NULL
subs.desc: Prevents NULL values from being stored in a column.

subs.label: CHECK
subs.desc: Validates column values against a boolean expression.

label: JOIN Queries
desc: Combining data from multiple tables using different join strategies.

subs.label: INNER JOIN
subs.desc: Returns rows where there is a match in both tables.

subs.label: LEFT JOIN
subs.desc: All rows from the left table, matched rows from the right (NULL if no match).

subs.label: RIGHT JOIN
subs.desc: All rows from the right table, matched rows from the left.

subs.label: FULL OUTER JOIN
subs.desc: All rows from both tables — NULLs where there is no match on either side.

subs.label: Self Join
subs.desc: Joining a table to itself — useful for hierarchical or comparison queries.

subs.label: Cross Join
subs.desc: Cartesian product of two tables — every row paired with every other row.

label: Subqueries
desc: Queries nested inside other queries — scalar, correlated, and derived tables.

subs.label: Nested Subqueries
subs.desc: Subqueries in WHERE, HAVING, or SELECT clauses — IN, EXISTS, ANY, ALL.

subs.label: Correlated Subqueries
subs.desc: Subqueries that reference columns from the outer query — evaluated per row.

subs.label: Scalar Subquery
subs.desc: Returns a single value — used in SELECT list or WHERE conditions.

label: Advanced Functions
desc: Built-in functions for string manipulation, math, dates, and conditional logic.

subs.label: String Functions
subs.desc: CONCAT, LENGTH, SUBSTRING, REPLACE, UPPER, LOWER, TRIM, LIKE.

subs.label: Math Functions
subs.desc: FLOOR, CEILING, ROUND, ABS, MOD — rounding and numeric operations.

subs.label: Date & Time Functions
subs.desc: DATE, TIME, TIMESTAMP, DATEPART, DATEADD — date arithmetic and formatting.

subs.label: CASE
subs.desc: Conditional logic inside SQL — simple CASE vs searched CASE.

subs.label: COALESCE / NULLIF
subs.desc: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL value; NULLIF returns NULL when two values are equal.

label: Views
desc: Virtual tables based on saved queries — simplifying complex queries and access control.

subs.label: Creating Views
subs.desc: CREATE VIEW — wrapping complex joins and logic into a reusable object.

subs.label: Modifying Views
subs.desc: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW and ALTER VIEW depending on the database.

subs.label: Dropping Views
subs.desc: DROP VIEW — removing views without affecting the underlying tables.

label: Indexes
desc: Data structures that speed up queries at the cost of write overhead and storage.

subs.label: Managing Indexes
subs.desc: CREATE INDEX, DROP INDEX, partial indexes, and covering indexes.

subs.label: Query Optimization with Indexes
subs.desc: How the query planner uses indexes — EXPLAIN / ANALYZE output.

label: Transactions
desc: Grouping SQL statements into atomic units of work that succeed or fail together.

subs.label: BEGIN
subs.desc: Starting a transaction — implicit vs explicit transaction management.

subs.label: COMMIT
subs.desc: Permanently saving all changes made in the current transaction.

subs.label: ROLLBACK
subs.desc: Undoing all changes since the last COMMIT or SAVEPOINT.

subs.label: SAVEPOINT
subs.desc: Creating a partial rollback point within a transaction.

subs.label: ACID
subs.desc: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — the four transaction guarantees.

subs.label: Transaction Isolation Levels
subs.desc: READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE.

label: Data Integrity & Security
desc: Protecting data correctness and controlling who can access what.

subs.label: Data Integrity Constraints
subs.desc: Entity, referential, and domain integrity — enforced at the DB level.

subs.label: GRANT and REVOKE
subs.desc: Managing user privileges — SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, EXECUTE.

subs.label: DB Security Best Practices
subs.desc: Least privilege, parameterised queries, auditing, encryption at rest.

label: Stored Procedures & Functions
desc: Reusable server-side logic stored in the database.

subs.label: Scalar Functions
subs.desc: Return a single value — used in SELECT lists and WHERE clauses.

subs.label: Table-valued Functions
subs.desc: Return a result set — inline and multi-statement variants.

subs.label: Row & Column Functions
subs.desc: Functions that operate per-row — window function foundations.

label: Performance Optimization
desc: Techniques to make SQL queries run faster at scale.

subs.label: Query Analysis Techniques
subs.desc: EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE — reading query plans, identifying bottlenecks.

subs.label: Using Indexes Effectively
subs.desc: Index selectivity, covering indexes, avoiding index scans on low-cardinality columns.

subs.label: Optimizing Joins
subs.desc: Join order, hash joins vs nested loop vs merge join.

subs.label: Reducing Subqueries
subs.desc: Rewriting correlated subqueries as joins or CTEs for better performance.

subs.label: Selective Projection
subs.desc: Selecting only needed columns — avoiding SELECT * in production queries.

label: Advanced SQL
desc: Power features for complex analytical and programmatic SQL work.

subs.label: Window Functions
subs.desc: OVER(), PARTITION BY, ROWS/RANGE — running totals, moving averages.

subs.label: RANK / DENSE_RANK / ROW_NUMBER
subs.desc: Ranking rows within partitions — differences and use cases.

subs.label: LEAD / LAG
subs.desc: Accessing values from the next or previous row within a partition.

subs.label: Common Table Expressions (CTEs)
subs.desc: WITH clause — making complex queries readable and enabling recursion.

subs.label: Recursive Queries
subs.desc: Recursive CTEs for hierarchical data — org charts, bill of materials.

subs.label: Pivot / Unpivot Operations
subs.desc: Transforming rows to columns and back — PIVOT, UNPIVOT, conditional aggregation.

subs.label: Dynamic SQL
subs.desc: Building and executing SQL strings at runtime — sp_executesql, EXECUTE.
